extra.reason: Workspace scaffolded and verified: cargo build/test/fmt/clippy clean on pinned 1.97.1, eio-signal builds for wasm32-unknown-unknown, lint baseline proven live by deliberate violation. Landed in f652004/0ca48c0/4f1dbe5 with the DAEMON-SPEC §1 + SCOPE §7.1 naming amendments. Follow-up eieio-u2m.3 filed for per-crate lint opt-in enforcement.

justfile landed with all recipes verified green and every gate proven to fail on a deliberate violation (std dep, missing lint opt-in, bad formatting, clippy warning). u2m.3 folded in as check-lint-optin, a dependency of lint. Commits 88f4358/6c2c5ee/db9fcee/753fd1a.

justfile landed with all recipes verified green and every gate proven to fail on a deliberate violation (std dep, missing lint opt-in, bad formatting, clippy warning). u2m.3 folded in as check-lint-optin, a dependency of lint. Commits 88f4358/6c2c5ee/db9fcee/753fd1a.

All 3 children complete. Epic criteria verified: cargo build/test succeed at the workspace root, justfile is the canonical developer+CI surface (just ci), and no_std enforcement for the leaf-shareable crates runs locally via just check-nostd against thumbv7em-none-eabihf and riscv32imc-unknown-none-elf.

signal crate landed: Value/Signal/Batch over a canonical CBOR profile, no_std+alloc, check-nostd green on both bare-metal targets. All acceptance criteria met and each new gate verified in the failing direction. Spec amendments landed in the same commit (e7a1995): ABI 6.3 value space closed, ABI 6.3.1 canonical form added with 11 rules and two documented RFC 8949 4.2.1 deviations, EXPR 2 float/map rows tightened. Follow-ups eieio-e6s.3 (typed decode errors) and eieio-e6s.4 (MAX_DEPTH configurability).

Property/round-trip suite and encoded-size accounting landed. Value/Signal/Batch::encoded_len is exact and computed structurally; 12 property tests cover round-trip, canonical fixed-point, length equality, and decoder totality over arbitrary bytes, CBOR-shaped bytes, mutations and truncations. Criterion 2's hand-written malformed-input cases were already delivered in e6s.1 and are strengthened here rather than duplicated. EXPR 9 MAX_VALUE_BYTES row amended in the same commit (d724591) to name the canonical encoding as the unit of measure. Follow-up eieio-e6s.5 filed.

Typed DecodeError landed (407f01a): one variant per ABI 6.3.1 rule, non_exhaustive, Display + core::error::Error, minicbor trait impls retained and bridged. All 52 rejection assertions converted from message substrings to variant matching, and proven discriminating by making two rules report the same variant. ABI 6.3.1 amended in the same commit to bound rejection-reason classification as diagnostic rather than normative.

Decided: configurable, recorded in ABI 6.3.1 rule 9 (0890aa0). Implemented as from_cbor_with_max_depth on Batch and Value with MIN_DEPTH floor clamping. The investigation also fixed a spec bug from e6s.1: rule 9 had required the bound be >= EXPR 9's reference default (128) rather than >= the host's configured expr MAX_DEPTH, which over-constrained exactly the leaf tier it was meant to protect.

Invariant documented and enforced (2a72fd4): every path from external bytes to a Value is depth-bounded, including the public minicbor Decode impls that bypass from_cbor. tests/depth.rs enforces it - pointing a trait impl at an unbounded decode aborts the test process, which is the hole it closes. Iterative impls rejected with evidence: impl Drop for Value fails E0509 and breaks Value destructuring this crate and expr both need, so Drop keeps recursing regardless and an iterative encoder would only move the crash.

All four epic acceptance criteria met and verified. (1) Value covers exactly the ABI 6.3 type space - all variants round-trip. (2) Signal is a text-keyed map, Batch an ordered array; the empty batch is legal and pins to 0x80. (3) minicbor round-trip encode/decode; crate is no_std + alloc and just check-nostd passes for both bare-metal targets, including the atomics-free riscv32imc. (4) Unit and property tests cover round-trips and edge cases - 52 tests across roundtrip/reject/properties/depth plus a doctest. Beyond the criteria the epic also produced ABI 6.3.1 (the normative canonical form, 11 rules with two documented RFC 8949 deviations), exact encoded-length accounting for EXPR 9's MAX_VALUE_BYTES, a typed DecodeError with a variant per rule, a host-configurable depth bound, and an enforced depth invariant. 5/5 children closed.

Lexer and parser landed (5abcf97 code+spec, 0104909 tests). Full EXPR 3.1 grammar with byte-offset spans on every node, ParseLimits floor-clamped per EXPR 9, the EXPR 8 error-code table, and the 5.2 let-shadowing check. EXPR 3.1 amended with a new 3.1.1 resolving seven ambiguities the grammar left open (letter=ASCII, the '-' tie-break, \u{1-6}, non-finite float literals, numbers running into symbols, one-expression-per-source, and parse-time budgets reporting PARSE). 36 tests, each rejection pinning code and span with an accepting near-miss alongside.

Static analysis landed (67682e1 code+spec, f066a5f tests). analyze/analyze_source expose signal-dependence classification plus collected diagnostics with spans; unbound detection handles let* sequential scoping (including the self-reference case that makes recursion unconstructible), fn params, and shadowed builtins. builtin.rs is the crate's single builtin-name table so s85.4's interpreter cannot diverge from it, checked against EXPR 7 independently in both directions. EXPR 5.2/5.4/10 amended: shape validation is required by unbound detection rather than optional, shadowing a special form and duplicate fn params are rejected, and diagnostics are collected.

Interpreter, builtin library and canonical rendering landed in 003b03c (code + EXPR 4/4.1/4.2/5.4/7/7.6/7.8/9 amendments) and b62e9e5 (87 tests). just ci green including no_std builds for both leaf targets. Seven deliberate breakages confirmed the tests bite.

Folded into eieio-s85.3 at that issue's scoping gate: all 63 builtins of EXPR 7.1-7.5 and 7.6's canonical rendering landed in 003b03c with their vectors in b62e9e5. The split was unsustainable — 4.2's equality IS the = builtin and 6 defines $name as sugar for a get. EXPR 7 gained an arity/fold-order convention and a new 7.8 Resolved details section; 7.6 was rewritten normatively.

EXPR 9 sharpened into 9.1 (bounded step accounting, FUEL not conformance-pinned) and 9.2 (clamping), a MAX_DEPTH accounting bug fixed so an expression nested to the budget both parses and evaluates, and 20 tests covering the floors, termination of every recursion in the crate, and 9's six determinism properties. 9cd3a53 + cb56825.

manifest crate landed: schema types, strict parsing, ABI 11.1 validation. just ci green including check-nostd on both bare-metal targets. Spec amendments (ABI 11.1, DAEMON 1 parser note) landed in the same push. Evidence and negative tests in the notes.

Resolved as part of eieio-m7o.3: ABI 4.4 now states that identity is equality of the PARSED manifests, not of the bytes, with the rationale (a registry entry reformatted by a publishing tool describes the same block). Implemented in eio_manifest::validate and covered both ways -- module.rs::reformatted_registry_manifest_agrees and module_reject.rs::embedded_and_registry_manifests_disagree. 4.4 additionally now rejects a module carrying two eio:manifest sections.

Module cross-check landed: all six ABI 4 checks with 16 distinct structured rejection reasons, 19 .wat fixtures, 29 tests. just ci green including check-nostd on both bare-metal targets. Spec amendments (4.2 both directions, 4.3 import names + MVP boundary, 4.4 identity + duplicate sections) landed in the same push. Notes carry the evidence, the negative tests, and a correction to the pre-implementation design note about wasmparser features.

expr-tests/ landed: 468 vectors in 12 JSON files, machine-enforced coverage of all 64 builtins, 5 special forms and 10 error codes, format documented normatively in expr-tests/README.md and referenced from EXPR 11. just ci green. Spec amendments (EXPR 11 pointer, EXPR 9 cross-reference, DAEMON 1 location fix) landed in the same push.

schemas/manifest.schema.json published (draft 2020-12), with bidirectional consistency tests over a 45-fixture corpus classified by what each side does with it, pattern-identity assertions against the crate's exported consts, and a documented-description gate. just ci green. ABI 11 records the location and the four rules JSON Schema cannot express.

Operands share values via Shared (borrowed / Rc / inline scalars); Signal stores its attributes as a Value so $ borrows them. Zero-copy proven by pointer identity for (get $ k) and for bindings holding a 4096-element array; fuel byte-identical across 32 expressions; Value/Signal/Batch/Expr/Analysis still Send+Sync. just ci green.

All seven children closed. The expr crate is no_std+alloc, implements EXPR §3-10 with code+span+message on every error, and expr-tests/ carries 468 host-agnostic vectors (expression + optional signal CBOR + expected value or error code) covering every builtin, special form, error code, the truthiness/equality tables, canonical-rendering pins, budget floors and signal-dependence classification.

ABI §11.1 now states which values satisfy which property type (int->float when exactly representable in binary64, decided by significant-bit count; float never satisfies int), and eio_manifest folds every signal-independent default and checks it, rejecting a contradiction with Error::DefaultTypeMismatch naming property, declared type and folded type. One implementation — PropertyType::accepts/conform — so host-core cannot diverge. Signal-dependent defaults unchecked; a fold that errors is not a manifest defect. Fixed ABI §11's example, which shipped a default that could never evaluate.

All five children closed. The manifest crate implements the full ABI §11 schema (property order = prop_id, port order = port indices), publishes schemas/manifest.schema.json tested in both directions against the Rust parser, cross-checks a module's import section per ABI §4.3 with capability-paired exports, and is no_std + alloc on both bare-metal targets.

crates/host-core lands the engine-agnostic ABI driver: the Engine trait (four methods, no instantiation, no engine types), the §5.1 lifecycle as typestate (Configured/Running/Stopped, every call consuming the instance, Stopped with no start), the §5.2 descriptor as canonical CBOR, §6.1/§9's delivery conventions including the alignment and refusal checks, and §8's three return conventions as three types with all nine error codes named. 59 tests against a mock engine, no wasmtime anywhere; no_std on both bare-metal targets. Amended ABI §9.5/§9.6 (a refused allocation is ERR_LIMIT and not fatal; a lying one is fatal) and §9.7 + SCOPE §3.4 (max_payload/max_batch have no floor, deliberately).

GitHub Actions runs 'just ci' and nothing else, green on main; the no_std gate runs in CI with all eight crate/target builds; cache configured and measured cold->warm (just ci 59s -> 14s, job 78s -> 35s); each of fmt/clippy/vector breakage verified to fail the gate locally, with the one gap — an observed red Actions check — recorded in the notes. workflow_dispatch added so an outage cannot leave main unverifiable.

Property evaluation protocol landed in crates/host-core/src/prop.rs (commit d27fcab), with the ABI 7.1 amendment in the same commit and the borrowing conform in d7e9595. All five acceptance criteria met and each proved by a test that fails when the mechanism is broken. just ci green including check-nostd on both bare-metal targets.

crates/daemon lands: wasmtime bound to host-core's Engine trait via a store-data dispatch table, all seven eio:core functions, and 'eio-daemon dev run-block' walking ABI 5.1 end to end over hand-built .wat blocks. Every acceptance criterion checked literally. Widened host-core's HostFn/HostCall to ABI 7's real shapes (Arg/Ret) and closed two spec silences it exposed: prop on an unset property is ERR_NOT_FOUND (ABI 7.1), and emit's three refusals are normative rather than host policy (ABI 6.2, implemented once in host-core as Outbound). Also clarified rand's return convention (ABI 7.0) and added DAEMON 5.1 (engine binding) and 12 (dev commands). Follow-ups: eieio-cq4, eieio-7sj.

Implemented in crates/daemon/src/props.rs::resolve as part of eieio-35h.3 — the --prop table is the first thing that reads a deployment, and the service-file parser (eieio-8yq.1) calls the same function. All three acceptance criteria covered by tests: a required property with neither a supplied value nor a default fails naming the property (props.rs a_required_property_with_neither_fails_and_names_itself, end_to_end a_required_property_with_no_value_fails_configuration_by_name); a default alone satisfies required (a_required_property_is_satisfied_by_its_default_alone); output is in manifest property order so prop_id matches the descriptor's props list (order_is_the_manifests_so_prop_ids_match_the_descriptor). Also settled the fourth combination ABI 11.1 admits and 7.1 was silent on: not required, no default, nothing supplied keeps its prop_id and answers ERR_NOT_FOUND. Where the function should LIVE is open as eieio-cq4.

Executor landed: one OS thread + one tokio task + bounded mailbox per instance, fuel and epoch budgets armed on every guest entry, death as a typed event. dev run-block rewired onto it. DAEMON 5/5.1 amended in the same commit (fbedbfd). 50 tests green, just ci green, every new gate proved able to fail.

Router landed: host-core owns the connection table, name->index resolution and fan-out (no_std, shared with the leaf per DAEMON 1); the daemon owns delivery -- bounded mailboxes, per-connection overflow, and the Service that wires every mailbox before any instance is spawned. Emissions route on the emitter's own thread after the callback returns (ABI 6.2), never off the unbounded event stream, which is what keeps backpressure real. DAEMON 6 rewritten normatively and its PROPOSED overflow default ratified in the same commit. All five acceptance criteria walked with tests, each new gate proven able to fail. Commits c692ea3, d959f51. Follow-ups: eieio-3r4, eieio-16g.

wasmtime Config now accepts core WASM MVP only, stated subtractively (all proposals off, then exactly WasmFeatures::MVP less GC_TYPES back on) so a proposal a future wasmtime enables by default is refused rather than silently admitted. Three tests: an MVP control, an 8-proposal refusal table each asserting the message names its proposal, and an end-to-end run of the new post_mvp.wat fixture proving eio_manifest accepts it while the engine refuses it. Both gates proven able to fail. DAEMON 5.1 rewritten (and a wrong recorded measurement about wasm_reference_types corrected), ABI 4.3 gained the MUST that a rejection name the proposal, SDK 5 gained -C target-feature=-bulk-memory. just ci green. Commit a901313.

Two permanent tests in crates/daemon/src/end_to_end.rs plus the new sink.wat fixture. echo.wat routes a signal to sink.wat, which evaluates a signal-dependent property ((+ $n 41) -> 42) against the routed batch and keeps an ABI 6.1 alloc/free ledger that eio_stop reports on. All four acceptance criteria walked literally; both new gates proven able to fail (expected value flipped; the deliberate-leak port neutralised). just ci green, 72 daemon tests pass. Commit 53602c4.

ABI 11.1 now reserves 'err' as a port name in BOTH inputs and outputs (widened from the issue's output-only framing at the gate: resolve_input rejects the name before consulting declared inputs, so an input named 'err' is equally unroutable). eio_manifest rejects it with Error::ReservedName, manifest.schema.json carries not:{const:'err'}, and both new fixtures sit in invalid/structural/ so schema and Rust are drift-tested against each other. Routes::resolve's ReservedOutputName removed with its test per the gate decision; DAEMON-SPEC 6 corrected to match, and Descriptor now documents the validated-manifest invariant the removal makes load-bearing. Both gates proven able to fail. just ci green. Commit 5652b9c.

ABI 11.1's required/default precedence moved from crates/daemon/src/props.rs (deleted) into crates/host-core/src/prop.rs, exported from the crate root and reachable from both hosts. Placement was structurally forced rather than a judgement call: resolve() consumes manifest's Manifest and produces host-core's PropertySource, and host-core depends on manifest, so no other crate can name both types. Pure move -- 8 tests moved verbatim and pass unchanged, which is the acceptance criterion; check-nostd proves it is genuinely leaf-compilable. DAEMON-SPEC 1 records the decision and why the other two homes were rejected. Commit f4ae930.

The lifecycle driver holds the PropContext and opens the scope at one choke point; process_signals takes the decoded batch and encodes it, so the guest's bytes and prop's signal_idx cannot be different batches. ABI 9.7's delivery half moved to host-core beside the emit half (gate decision), recorded in DAEMON 1. prop.rs unchanged; four new scope tests each proven to fail when the mechanism is removed.

Delivery goes through a per-service registry of each instance's current mailbox, read per delivery, so replacing an instance replaces the mailbox every peer uses next. Service::restart is DAEMON 8's mechanism (policy stays OPEN): stop and join the old, install the new mailbox before spawning, fresh eio_configure from a retained compiled Module. Chain test a->b->c restarts b and c still receives; proven to fail red when the senders are baked at spawn time. DAEMON 5 corrected, 6 and 8 state the indirection.

expr-tests/properties/ is a second host-agnostic suite carrying the declared property type alongside the expression and asserting the value a guest decodes, run by crates/host-core/tests/properties.rs where both halves of the rule meet. The int-vs-float question needed no decision: ABI 11.1 already states it normatively and PropertyType::accepts/conform is the single implementation both call sites use. The exemption is reworded in EXPR 11, the README and the runner, and properties/ has a coverage audit of its own.
Resolved by eieio-35h.8: guest_with, prop and batch now live in crates/host-core/tests/mock.rs and prop.rs uses them, so the duplicated helper is gone.
Duplicate of eieio-p0k.3, filed because I did not list the epic's children before creating issues. Its content is folded into p0k.3's notes.
Duplicate of eieio-p0k.4, filed for the same reason. Its content is folded into p0k.4's notes.

Value::to_cbor and Batch::to_cbor pre-size from encoded_len(); drift guard asserts capacity()==len() over generated values and at every CBOR head-width boundary. Both directions of hint drift proven to fail the new gate. just ci green. Landed in ed6d781.

EXPR §10 gained a MUST-reject for a list whose head is a literal or a sigil, with 8 new vectors (468→476) and the two (1 2) TYPE vectors re-pointed at an undecidable list head. Both halves of the rule proven to fail independently when removed. The rule caught five pre-existing instances of the mistake it was written for, all in manifest examples and fixtures. Landed in 155185f and b825078.

Runner now asserts a biconditional: a parseable vector is statically rejected iff it expects ANY. EXPR §10 item 3 promoted SHOULD→MUST to resolve the section's self-contradiction; three vectors that pinned a diagnostic code flipped to ANY; UNBOUND's coverage moved to the ANY vectors' reference diagnostics. Proven by deleting an analyze rule and watching its vector go red — the exact case that was silently green before. Landed in 41e9b3d.

EXPR §10 now decides argument counts for a directly-named builtin, dict's pairing, and a fn written where it is applied; the MUST NOT half leaves value-dependent counts to evaluation. dict's rule moved from collect::dict into Arity::pairs. §10's contradicting MAY clause deleted. 9 vectors flipped to ANY, 8 added (476→484). Each rule proven by removal. Landed in 51ce5ae and 66e6bed.

compile now collects every property that fails parse or static analysis in one pass, in prop_id order, each with its name and EXPR §8 code. CompileError holds the list (non-empty by construction); PropertyError is the per-property fault. Single-failure Display unchanged. Proven by restoring the early return. Follow-up eieio-35h.14 filed for the identical bail in manifest validation. Landed in 0e570da.

Budgets holds the expression and decode budgets together with rule 9's floor enforced at construction; Outbound::decode takes it rather than a bare u32 so no call site can name a violating bound; the daemon builds one per instance feeding both the prop compile and emit's decode. eio-signal's rustdoc now points at the structural home. Proven by breaking the clamp and, separately, the plumbing. Landed in 2033521 and 6f91e2e.

echo, canary, emitter and probe now free every host-allocated payload, following sink.wat's pattern, with free-after-emit ordering stated at each site; spinner, trapper and the four load-refused fixtures carry a comment naming why §6.1 does not apply. echo's misleading 'which is legal' comment corrected. Proven reached by trapping echo's eio_free. Landed in 3744b04.

Error::InvalidDefaults(Vec<InvalidDefault>) collects every default that fails parse or static analysis, in declaration order, each with its name and EXPR §8 code; single-failure Display byte-identical. Two passes keep analysis failures ahead of type mismatches. Proven by breaking the collection and the precedence separately. Landed in 9cf5ef2.

memory_range exported from host-core; daemon's private range() deleted and the mock's four open-coded copies replaced; wraparound test moved into host-core and made able to fail (it could not before, on any 64-bit host). Helper hardened to checked_add. Landed in 32c7a74.

Exit milestone met and verified in code: host-core (no_std, cross-built for both MCU targets), the task-per-instance executor with fuel/epoch budgets, the router with fan-out and emit-enqueue semantics, and an end-to-end test routing a signal between two real WASM instances with a balanced ABI 6.1 ledger and a negative companion. All 18 remaining children closed; the two stragglers were follow-ups on later epics and were reparented out of a dependency cycle that had frozen 39 issues.

eio-sdk exists as a guest runtime: dlmalloc behind eio_alloc/eio_free with ABI 9.6's alignment, a panic handler that logs before it traps, Ctx wrapping all seven eio:core imports with the grow-and-retry loop hidden, and HostError/BlockError preserving ABI 8 codes as matchable variants. All five acceptance criteria walked against the code; every new gate broken deliberately and confirmed to fail. SDK 2 and 4 expanded to normative prose and 4's PROPOSED allocator ratified, landing with the code. Follow-ups filed as eieio-7d8.13 and eieio-7d8.14.
